what_happened: Root-caused the sentinel self-collision to one predicate (scopes_overlap_first's exact-match clause in scripts/lib/file-scope-overlap.sh) and confirmed via direct code reading that fixing it there reaches both named consumers (orchestrate-batch-admit.sh, lint-roadmap-batch-proposals.sh) with zero parallel edit needed in the lint consumer. Also found the actual width-1-serialization mechanism is orchestrate-cycle-plan.sh's whole_tree_claim case arm having no --allow-X bypass, and found an existing TDD fixture (WHOLE-TREE-CODISPATCH in test-orchestrate-batch-admit.sh) whose target-posture assertions must be explicitly flipped since this is a deliberate design reversal, not a latent-bug fix.

Dispatch description's central premise is false against live state: it asserts WHOLE-TREE-CODISPATCH in scripts/tests/test-orchestrate-batch-admit.sh is RED today and that orchestrate-batch-admit.sh emits defer_reason file_scope_collision with overlapping_path __WHOLE_TREE__ for the sentinel-vs-sentinel case. Measured: the suite runs 15 passed, 0 failed, WHOLE-TREE-CODISPATCH among the passes; the whole_tree_claim branch already exists at orchestrate-batch-admit.sh lines 1070-1105 and already emits defer_reason whole_tree_claim with claim_sentinel, colliding_task_number and collision_scope. The named deliverable is already satisfied. The research report ALSO described a different (pre-narrowing) framing. The only measurably-unmet requirement in the description is its REGRESSION clause: a probe shows the concrete-path collision is masked as a bare whole_tree_claim whenever the sentinel precedes the shared concrete path in the declared file_scope array (declaration-order-dependent). Plan was re-scoped to that clause alone.

Running the named fixture suite and a two-ordering probe against a byte-for-byte copy of the live admit script in an isolated temp root cost about five tool calls and definitively settled a premise the dispatch description, the research report, and the fixture's own header comment each stated differently. The probe also surfaced the real, still-open defect (declaration-order-dependent masking of a concrete-path collision) that no document named, and the schema doc's own sentence 'no change to which peer is selected or why' then picked the fix shape by ruling out the cross-peer variant. Measuring before planning replaced three conflicting narratives with one measurement.

Phase 1's new WHOLE-TREE-REAL-PATH-PRECEDENCE fixture (sub-cases A/B) produced the exact RED-for-the-right-reason baseline the plan predicted on first run: sub-case A (concrete path declared first) passed silently, sub-case B (sentinel declared first) failed on exactly the three predicted fields (defer_reason, overlapping_path, claim_sentinel), and all 15 pre-existing cases stayed green by name.

Deliberately left unclosed (plan Non-Goal): the new scopes_overlap_first_preferring_concrete precedence applies PER-PEER, not across peers. A candidate overlapping one peer A only on the reserved __WHOLE_TREE__ sentinel and a DIFFERENT peer B only on a real concrete path can still have $hit select peer A (if A sorts first in the admitted-set-only in_batch scan), reporting defer_reason whole_tree_claim even though a real-path collision exists against a different peer B. This is the same masking CLASS one level up (across peers rather than within one pair), explicitly not closed here: closing it would change WHICH PEER $hit names, which docs/architecture/batch-admit-schema.md's precedence paragraph asserts is unchanged ('no change to which peer is selected or why') and which the dispatch's 'every other comparison shape MUST be preserved exactly' forbids.
